text: {"features":[{"name":"Software engineering depth","description":"Shows the extent and relevance of the candidate's hands-on production software experience across testing, maintenance, launches, and service ownership.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Presents only the minimum threshold of relevant experience, with limited scope such as a few years and little sense of repeated production ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows modest but relevant production experience, typically a few years with some testing, maintenance, and launch exposure."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows solid professional depth, with multiple years in production environments and clear responsibility for more than one service."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong production depth, with five or more years or repeated ownership across several services through the full lifecycle."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows extensive and clearly relevant production depth, pairing substantial tenure with repeated launch, maintenance, and ownership of multiple production systems at meaningful scale."}]},{"name":"Go back-end depth","description":"Shows how specifically and credibly the letter connects the candidate's Go experience to back-end engineering work relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mentions Go only briefly or as one language among several, without tying it to concrete back-end responsibility."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Identifies Go as a regular or primary language but gives little detail about what was built with it."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Links Go to concrete production services or back-end work the candidate has built or maintained."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Uses Go in clearly role-relevant systems such as automation pipelines, internal platforms, or security tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows strong ownership of designing Go back-end infrastructure that constrains, audits, or scales security-related automation."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"Shows the depth and relevance of the candidate's Python experience for automation, services, analysis, or agent work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no meaningful evidence of Python use."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python generically or as a secondary language without examples of substantive work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or internal services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong Python responsibility across services, scripts, or analysis systems used by others."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows deep Python experience that is central to production agentic or security automation systems."}]},{"name":"AI production maturity","description":"Shows whether the letter presents AI experience as real production engineering rather than a vague interest or buzzword.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Makes no meaningful case for AI experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Refers to AI only vaguely or as interest rather than delivered work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that the candidate built or shipped AI or LLM-backed features."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Adds concrete production concerns such as evaluation, hardening, trustworthiness, or handling failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows mature AI engineering judgment by pairing shipped systems with explicit safeguards, evaluation practices, and a reliability-first mindset."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems design","description":"Shows how clearly the letter demonstrates experience designing agent-based systems with real architectural ownership.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention agents or autonomous workflows."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents or automation in broad terms without architectural detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a recognizable agentic pattern, such as Python agents paired with Go services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains how agents are bounded through permissions, guardrails, logging, or auditability."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic system design, including clear control boundaries, orchestration choices, and production constraints."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability triage automation","description":"Shows the extent to which the letter demonstrates direct experience automating vulnerability intake, routing, and handling workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence of automating vulnerability handling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions automation generally but not in the context of vulnerability reports or triage."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that the candidate automated intake or triage of vulnerability reports."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Adds concrete functions such as classification, routing, prioritization, or deduplication that reduce manual work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents a robust vulnerability-handling system with multiple triage functions and a clear operational effect on team capacity or response speed."}]},{"name":"Security assessment depth","description":"Shows the depth of hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues and following through on findings.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no direct evidence of security assessment work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Signals security interest but does not describe hands-on assessment activity."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions having reviewed or assessed services for security issues."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Specifies concrete assessment methods such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or validation of fixes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows substantial hands-on assessment depth across systems, with an attacker-minded approach and explicit follow-through to remediation."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"Shows how convincingly the letter demonstrates practical strength with data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Offers no meaningful evidence of data structures or algorithmic problem solving."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims algorithmic strength in general terms without an example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides one concrete example of using a better data structure or algorithm to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Provides a strong example of redesigning a bottlenecked system through a specific algorithmic or structural change."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows especially convincing practical algorithmic strength through highly relevant, clearly explained redesigns that materially changed system behavior or scale."}]},{"name":"Role understanding","description":"Shows how specifically the letter understands the actual responsibilities and challenges of this security automation role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Reads as applicable to many software roles and shows little grasp of this team's specific work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Echoes one or two job-posting terms but does not develop a clear picture of the actual responsibilities."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a basic understanding of the role by referencing several relevant activities such as security tooling, vulnerability response, or AI agents."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear understanding of the job as building systems that automate security processes and support developer teams at scale."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows deep understanding of the role by framing it as a systems problem involving triage, variant analysis, bounded automation, and secure defaults across a large engineering organization."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"Shows whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers work safely with less friction.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not address how the work should help product engineers or frames security mainly as oversight."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions helping teams in general terms but without a clear philosophy of enablement."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that security tooling should make secure development easier for developers."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Emphasizes reducing friction, staying close to users, or building defaults that busy engineers will actually follow."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes developer enablement a core theme, showing that success comes from making the secure path the easy path through thoughtful tooling."}]},{"name":"Platform leverage orientation","description":"Shows how strongly the letter is motivated by the platform-wide and organization-wide leverage of the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows little interest in the platform-wide or organization-wide nature of the work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Google scale or impact only as a generic attraction."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Expresses clear interest in foundational systems or work whose benefits spread broadly."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Connects central infrastructure work to multiplier effects across many teams or products."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes platform leverage a defining reason for applying, with a compelling explanation of why inherited downstream impact fits the candidate's goals."}]},{"name":"Security motivation","description":"Shows how personally and credibly the letter explains why the candidate wants to work in security engineering.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives little or no personal reason for wanting to work in security engineering."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses generic enthusiasm for security impact without a distinctive rationale."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides a plausible personal reason for preferring security-oriented engineering."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Articulates a clear security philosophy centered on prevention, resilience, or secure development by default."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes security motivation feel deeply internalized by linking prior experiences, values, and future direction to the mission of preventing incidents before they happen."}]},{"name":"Security credibility signals","description":"Shows the strength of external or extra-role signals that the candidate has invested in practical security capability.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Adds no meaningful security signal beyond general interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows introductory self-study or broad curiosity but no stronger external validation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides a baseline credibility signal such as Security+ or regular participation in security exercises."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Provides a strong hands-on signal such as OSCP or consistently strong capture-the-flag performance."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Provides multiple strong signals of security depth, combining advanced credentials, offensive practice, or similarly concrete evidence of hands-on capability."}]},{"name":"Engineering rigor","description":"Shows whether the letter presents the candidate as someone who builds dependable, bounded, and production-safe systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Makes few or no claims about correctness, reliability, auditability, or production discipline."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Uses general quality language without showing how rigor appears in practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions at least one concrete rigor signal such as trustworthy behavior, production standards, or reliable deployment concerns."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows several concrete rigor mechanisms such as testing, typing, evaluations, guardrails, auditing, or fix verification."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents rigor as a defining working style, repeatedly grounding claims in specific mechanisms that make systems dependable, bounded, and safe in production."}]},{"name":"Open-source engagement","description":"Shows the extent to which the letter demonstrates contribution to or stewardship of open-source software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of open-source contribution."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions open source only passively or as usage rather than contribution."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows occasional upstream contributions such as submitting fixes when professional work uncovers defects."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows sustained open-source contribution or meaningful maintenance responsibility."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows substantial open-source leadership, such as maintaining a project or library with reviews, releases, and outside users or contributors."}]},{"name":"Personal technical initiative","description":"Shows how strongly the letter demonstrates self-directed technical work beyond assigned job duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of technical initiative outside assigned work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small side project or hobby build with limited technical ambition."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows a completed personal project that demonstrates follow-through and some relevant engineering skill."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows a substantial self-directed project chosen to explore hard systems or security problems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows exceptional initiative through an ambitious personal system with clearly described edge cases, semantics, recovery behavior, or production-grade discipline."}]},{"name":"Evidence specificity","description":"Shows how consistently the letter supports its claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, and outcomes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on generic claims and adjectives with little concrete support."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Provides some examples but leaves important claims vague or unsupported."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Uses several concrete examples of work, though the scope or effect is only partly explained."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently supports claims with specific systems, responsibilities, or improvements."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Builds credibility through repeated concrete examples that explain what was built, how it worked, and what difference it made."}]},{"name":"Narrative coherence","description":"Shows how well the letter turns qualifications into a clear, persuasive case for fit with this specific role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Feels like a disconnected list of qualifications rather than a reasoned case for fit."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has a basic structure but weakly connects motivation, experience, and the target role."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents a coherent overall case, even if some sections read as separate points."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Develops a clear through-line showing how prior work naturally leads to this role."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Delivers a tightly integrated argument in which motivation, evidence, and role fit reinforce one another from opening to close."}]},{"name":"Writing mechanics","description":"Shows the level of proofreading, grammatical control, and sentence-level polish in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Contains frequent spelling or grammar errors that noticeably distract from the substance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Contains regular errors that weaken polish but do not seriously block comprehension."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Contains some noticeable errors yet remains generally clear and professional."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Contains only minor mechanical issues and reads as polished overall."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is essentially error-free, carefully proofread, and consistently polished at the sentence level."}]}]}
